Friday, November 6

Game recap

UTA4MTL5OTFinal: UTA 4, MTL 5 OT

Logan Cooley scored a hat trick and added an assist, Utah led three separate times, and the Mammoth still flew out of Montreal with one point. Cooley went 9, 10, 11 on the season, two of them on the power play, and Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal made it 4-3 early in the third. Every time, the Canadiens came back: Nick Suzuki (a goal, two assists), Arber Xhekaj, who scored his first and then dropped the gloves with Liam O'Brien four seconds later, Kirby Dach, and Adam Engstrom, whose first of the year tied it 4-4 with five minutes left. Cole Caufield needed 30 seconds of overtime for his 11th, set up by Lane Hutson and Suzuki. Jakub Dobes stopped only 16 of 20, Sebastian Cossa 30 of 35. Montreal is 10-3-3. Utah held the lead for most of the night and handed it back three times: that's not a lead, that's a timeshare.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK2DET1Final: VGK 2, DET 1

Forty minutes of nothing, then a third period worth the price of admission, and Vegas took it 2-1 in Detroit. Anton Johansson finally broke the ice for the Red Wings two minutes into the third, and the lead lasted all of 2:18 before Braeden Bowman tied it. Then, with 1:42 left, Trevor Connelly buried his seventh from Jack Eichel and Rasmus Andersson, and the Little Caesars Arena crowd went home with cold pizza. Carter Hart was the reason it got that far, stopping 25 of 26, while Daniil Tarasov made 32 saves on 34 shots in a game the Wings had no business staying in. Vegas is 11-5-2. Detroit falls to 7-7-3, one goal on a night it needed two. Hockeytown has been rebuilding so long the blueprints are on microfiche.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI1TBL4Final: CHI 1, TBL 4

Tampa Bay is now 8-0 at home, and Chicago never looked like the team to change that. Victor Hedman opened it on the power play four minutes in, Ilya Mikheyev scored late in the first, and early in the third Ryan McDonagh and Mikheyev again made it 4-0 inside three minutes. Zemgus Girgensons came back from his lower-body injury ahead of schedule and set up Mikheyev's second. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26, and the one he missed was Roman Kantserov's with 50 seconds left, which is the closest thing to a highlight the Blackhawks had. Dillon Boucher and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the second. Arvid Soderblom made 31 saves on 35 shots. The Lightning are 10-3-2. Chicago is 4-12-1, and in a rebuild like this, spoiling the shutout counts as a win.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL4NJD5OTFinal: STL 4, NJD 5 OT

New Jersey led 4-1 after two periods and still needed Jesper Bratt in overtime. The Devils built it with a goal from Luke Hughes, two from Anthony Mantha and one from Jesper Boqvist, with Mantha's second coming 19 seconds after Boqvist's; Jack Hughes had two assists. Then St. Louis woke up. Mason McTavish scored midway through the third, Philip Broberg made it 4-3, and Dalibor Dvorsky tied it 18 seconds later with 5:06 to go. Bratt settled it 1:26 into overtime, from Dougie Hamilton. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 28 of 32, and Jordan Binnington made 31 saves on 36 shots. Jake Neighbours and Timo Meier fought early in the second. The Devils are 11-5-0. The Blues scored three goals in 3:08 to rescue a game they'd spent two periods losing, then got a loser point for it, which is the most St. Louis outcome possible.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR5NYI3Final: CAR 5, NYI 3

Carolina scored twice in the first 3:20, the Islanders tied it twice, and the league's best team won it anyway, 5-3 at UBS Arena. Logan Stankoven scored 57 seconds in and Jesperi Kotkaniemi added another. Mitchell Chaffee (his first) and Brayden Schenn tied it early in the second; Andrei Svechnikov put Carolina back in front a minute later, and Victor Eklund tied it again before the second intermission. The winner came from the least likely name on the sheet: William Carrier, his first of the season with 5:08 left, from Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho. Jalen Chatfield added the empty-netter. Brandon Bussi stopped 24 of 27, Semyon Varlamov 34 of 38. The Hurricanes are 13-3-2. The Islanders, still without Mathew Barzal and Ryan Pulock, are 7-6-2, and they made their fans watch a fourth-liner decide it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI2NYR3Final: PHI 2, NYR 3

Philadelphia had a third-period lead at Madison Square Garden and gave it back in 89 seconds. Gabe Perreault scored first for the Rangers, then Simon Benoit (his first of the year) and Noel Acciari scored two minutes apart in the second to put the Flyers up 2-1. It held until 13:52 of the third, when Pavel Dorofeyev tied it on the power play, and Tye Kartye won it at 15:21, with Adam Fox assisting on both. Dylan Garand stopped 23 of 25 for New York, and Joseph Woll made 25 saves on 28 shots for Philadelphia. The Rangers are 9-7-1. The Flyers fall to 4-10-4. For an offense that scores less than anyone, two goals is a hot streak, and they still couldn't hold it through the third.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS6PIT2Final: BOS 6, PIT 2

Justin Brazeau gave Pittsburgh a 1-0 lead nine minutes in, and Boston answered with six of the next seven goals. Pavel Zacha, Mark Kastelic and Elias Lindholm, unassisted, scored in the last eight minutes of the first. Nick Robertson got the Penguins back within 3-2 early in the second, then Zacha scored again, Morgan Geekie made it 5-2 and Fraser Minten added the sixth in the third. David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka each had two assists, both on Zacha's goals. Michael DiPietro only had to stop 16 of 18. At the other end, Arturs Silovs saw 24 shots and stopped 18, which is how you get to 5-9-2. The Bruins are 12-4-1. Pittsburgh's lead lasted three minutes and its defense never showed up, which is about how this season has gone for a franchise that keeps insisting it isn't rebuilding.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL1CBJ2SOFinal: DAL 1, CBJ 2 SO

Two goalies, 65 minutes and one goal each, and Columbus won the skills competition. Cam Talbot and Casey DeSmith made it scoreless through two periods, and Mikko Rantanen's ninth, from Wyatt Johnston, looked like enough for Dallas midway through the third. Then Zach Werenski scored his first goal of the season with 3:14 left, from Kent Johnson and Matthew Knies, and the Blue Jackets never trailed again. In the shootout Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scored; Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin didn't. Talbot finished with 27 saves on 28 shots plus both shootout attempts, and DeSmith stopped 29 of 30. Columbus is 7-7-0 with two straight wins. Dallas, without Miro Heiskanen, is 9-5-2. The Stars put one puck past Talbot in 65 minutes and none in the shootout, and that offense couldn't pass a referendum either.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2WPG6Final: VAN 2, WPG 6

Winnipeg went nine games without a win; now it has two in a row, and Vancouver was happy to help. Alex Iafallo scored on the power play at 3:49 and Cole Koepke added another 14 seconds later. Liam Ohgren answered for the Canucks, but Dawson Mercer scored his first of the season before the first intermission, Neal Pionk and Mark Scheifele scored in the second, and Mario Ferraro made it 6-1 in the third. Kyle Connor and Dylan DeMelo each had two assists, and Scheifele had a goal and an assist. Brock Boeser scored late. Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 26 for the Jets, and Leevi Meriläinen gave up six on 29 shots. Winnipeg is 6-8-3. Vancouver is 3-14-1, the league's worst, and has become the team you play when you need to feel good about yourself again.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5EDM4Final: ANA 5, EDM 4

Pavel Mintyukov had the full Gordie Howe hat trick, and Anaheim held on in Edmonton, 5-4. Cutter Gauthier opened it on the power play, Evan Bouchard answered on one, and Connor McDavid scored shorthanded early in the second to make it 2-1 Oilers. Then the Ducks scored four straight: Mintyukov twice, his first two of the season, three minutes apart, and Beckett Sennecke twice, the second on the power play early in the third. Mintyukov also set up Sennecke's first and fought Kasperi Kapanen in the first period. Edmonton came back late: Kapanen on the power play, then Leon Draisaitl at 19:15 with the goalie pulled, but time ran out. McDavid had a goal and two assists. Laurent Brossoit stopped 23 of 27; Matt Tomkins 16 of 21. Edmonton is 11-3-3. Five goals on 21 shots: the Oilers' goaltending search goes on, now in its second decade.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3COL2OTFinal: NSH 3, COL 2 OT

Nashville goes past regulation again, and this time Steven Stamkos made it count. Ross Colton opened the scoring, Jaden Schwartz tied it, Vitali Pinchuk put the Predators back in front with his first of the season, and Parker Kelly tied it early in the second. After that, nothing for 37 minutes, until Stamkos scored on the power play 2:18 into overtime, from Roman Josi and Ryan O'Reilly. Justus Annunen was the story in the Nashville net, stopping 30 of 32 at Ball Arena, while Mackenzie Blackwood made 22 saves on 25 shots. Colorado tried a new top pair, with Sam Malinski beside Devon Toews and Cale Makar moved to Brett Kulak's side, and got two goals out of 32 shots for the trouble. The Predators are 7-4-5. The Avalanche, 9-6-2, have one of the league's best attacks and got outscored by Vitali Pinchuk and Ross Colton.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Thursday, November 5

Game recap

OTT2BUF1Final: OTT 2, BUF 1

Buffalo came home from a California sweep, led for most of the night, and still found a way to be Buffalo. Peyton Krebs put the Sabres up 1-0 at 14:00 of the second, his first of the season, off Tage Thompson and Zach Benson, and for a while Colten Ellis looked like he'd make it stand. Then the third period happened. Shane Pinto tied it at 11:33 from Philip Tomasino and Thomas Chabot, and Michael Amadio won it at 16:51 off Tim Stützle and Fabian Zetterlund: two goals in five minutes and change. Samuel Ersson stopped 23 of 24 for Ottawa, which had dropped three of four last week and needed this one. Ellis made 28 saves on 30 shots and deserved better. Ottawa is 10-6-1 and third in the Atlantic. Buffalo just learned that a one-goal lead in the third is only a rental, and Sabres fans have seen that lease run out before.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI3FLA5Final: CHI 3, FLA 5

Sandis Vilmanis played 13 minutes and 32 seconds and put up four points, a night's work most top-six forwards would frame. The Panthers won 5-3: Vilmanis opened the scoring at 4:43, Carter Verhaeghe made it 2-0 on the power play and Seth Jones made it 3-0 in the second. Chicago, to its credit, made it interesting. Roman Kantserov got one back, Frank Nazar scored shorthanded and then again at 16:09 of the third to make it 4-3, with Connor Bedard assisting twice. But Vilmanis had already scored his second at 11:01, and Sam Reinhart's empty-netter at 18:33 closed it. Jacob Markstrom stopped 17 of 20; Spencer Knight made 25 saves on 29. Florida is 9-5-2 and 7-3-0 in its last 10. The Blackhawks are 4-11-1 and -27, which is a rebuild in the same way a house fire is a renovation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS2LAK7Final: SJS 2, LAK 7

Adrian Kempe walked back into the lineup and treated the Sharks like a practice dummy. Kempe scored 83 seconds in, again at 16:09 of the first, and completed the hat trick on a second-period power play, with an assist for a four-point night. Artemi Panarin had four assists, Quinton Byfield scored twice on the power play, and Erik Haula and Joel Armia piled on in a 7-2 Kings romp. Three of the seven came on the power play, which San Jose's penalty kill mostly watched. Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg scored for San Jose, both on the power play, but Yaroslav Askarov stopped just 20 of 27, and Darcy Kuemper made 30 saves on 32. The Kings are 5-7-2 and climbing out of their hole. The Sharks lost a third straight, their fifth in six, and held a players-only meeting afterward. Bring snacks, fellas: at this rate it's going to be a standing reservation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1SEA2OTFinal: CGY 1, SEA 2 OT

Two goalies spent 60 minutes refusing to let anything happen, and then Matty Beniers decided he had somewhere to be. Beniers scored 55 seconds into overtime off Brandon Montour, and Seattle beat Calgary 2-1. Yegor Sharangovich opened the scoring at 12:45 of the first, and the Flames sat on that lead until Berkly Catton tied it at 13:09 of the second, stretching his point streak to seven games. After that it was Joey Daccord (25 saves on 26) and Dustin Wolf (27 on 29) trading stops until the 3-on-3 broke it open. Seattle is 9-5-1 and third in the Pacific. Calgary takes a point and is 7-8-1, scoring 2.44 goals a game, and the Saddledome goal horn is starting to wonder if it still has a job.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Friedman: teams expect Kucherov not to sign anywhere before July 1, even if Tampa trades him

On 32 Thoughts, Elliotte Friedman said the impression around the league is that Kucherov will wait for free agency, and that he hasn't sent Tampa a list of teams he would sign an extension with after a trade. Friedman added he wouldn't bet much on it. Agent Dan Milstein has said Kucherov will sign with a new club on July 1 whether he's traded now or later.

Trade rumorNot confirmed by the team

Russo: Wild have made their best offer to Detroit for Dylan Larkin and likely won't add to it

Speaking on The Sheet, The Athletic's Michael Russo said Minnesota's offer for Larkin is built on futures: a young player, a veteran under contract and multiple first-round picks. He said Eriksson Ek and Boldy won't be traded, that Brodin can't be moved with Spurgeon and Faber out, and that nothing is imminent.

San Jose (7-9-1) held a players-only meeting after losing 7-2 to the Kings. Kiefer Sherwood called the performance 'unacceptable' and said the coaches aren't to blame, and coach Ryan Warsofsky said he appreciated the leaders stepping up. The Sharks finish the trip in Minnesota on Friday.

Beniers scores 55 seconds into overtime as the Kraken beat Calgary 2-1; Catton's point streak reaches seven games

Matty Beniers scored on a breakaway after a Brandon Montour interception, and Joey Daccord made 25 saves. Berkly Catton tied it in the second, stretching his point streak to seven games, the longest this season by a player 20 or younger.

LAK 3–0 BOS

Los Angeles KingsLAK6-11-2 · 14 pts22 shots
3
FinalTD Garden
0
Boston BruinsBOS13-7-1 · 27 pts29 shots
1st2nd3rdTLAK1113BOS0000

Puckline's Report

Darcy Kuemper walked into TD Garden, stopped all 29 shots for his 40th career shutout, then picked up an assist on the empty-netter, which means the Kings' goalie outscored the entire Bruins roster. Mats Zuccarello opened the scoring late in the first off a feed from Erik Gustafsson, who was back after three games out. Andre Lee made it 2-0 late in the second, and Gustafsson finished it into the empty net with Kuemper getting the helper. Los Angeles ends a four-game losing streak. Michael DiPietro did his part, 19 saves on 21, and got the run support of a man jogging alone. Marco Sturm reunited David Pastrnak, Elias Lindholm and Morgan Geekie, and the reunion tour sold zero tickets. That's three straight losses for Boston, which now heads to Detroit's centennial party as the guest who forgot to bring a gift, or a goal.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

Connor McDavid ran his point streak to 23 games and passed Wayne Gretzky for the Oilers' record in power-play points along the way, the kind of sentence you only get to write about one guy. Edmonton was up 4-0 before Florida found the building: Kasperi Kapanen opened it, McDavid scored on the power play, and Vasily Podkolzin scored twice in the second, his 11th and 12th, one of them on the power play too. Podkolzin, Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl all finished with three points. Matthew Tkachuk scored twice in the last seven minutes to push his own point streak to nine games, and Draisaitl's 21st into the empty net ended the suspense. Devon Levi stopped 20 of 22. Jacob Markstrom stopped 13 of 17, a .765 that plays as a batting average and nowhere else. The Panthers took almost 54 minutes to show up to their own home game, which in South Florida still counts as early.

Puckline's Report

Matthew Schaefer scored his first career hat trick, the first by an Islanders defenseman since Denis Potvin in 1982, and when the comparison is Potvin you can stop the scouting report there. He scored unassisted early in the second for a 2-0 lead, restored the two-goal cushion in the third after Zach Werenski had cut it to 2-1, and finished into the empty net, his ninth of the season on nine shots on goal for the night. Anthony Duclair opened the scoring on a power play with 58 seconds left in the first, Tony DeAngelo added one, Mathew Barzal had two assists, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 28 of 29. Cam Talbot faced 40 shots, stopped 36 and should file for hazard pay. That's five straight regulation losses for Columbus. The Blue Jackets have finally found consistency. It's just the wrong kind.

Puckline's Report

The Sabres led 47 seconds in, led again midway through the second, and lost anyway, because Buffalo handles a lead like a hot pan. Mattias Samuelsson opened the scoring, Jamie Drysdale tied it, Tage Thompson's 13th put Buffalo back in front, and Owen Tippett tied it again. Travis Sanheim gave Philadelphia its first lead 29 seconds into the third, Jiri Kulich answered with his first goal in 11 games, and Christian Dvorak won it 52 seconds after that. Matvei Michkov's two assists stretched his point streak to five games. Nobody is framing the goalie lines: Joseph Woll stopped 16 of 19 and won, Alex Lyon stopped 29 of 33 and didn't. Outshot 33-19 and still tied in the third, the Sabres found the most Buffalo way to get nothing. Five straight losses, and it's mid-November with fans already checking the lottery odds, the one annual tradition this franchise never misses.

Puckline's Report

Tyler Boucher, the 10th overall pick in 2021, waited five years for his first NHL game and then scored the winner in it, which is one way to make up for lost time. Ottawa got both of its goals 58 seconds apart early in the second: Drake Batherson's 11th on the power play, then Boucher off a pass from Thomas Chabot. Winnipeg's Viggo Björck answered with his own first NHL goal five minutes later, and that was the end of the scoring, with more than half the game still to play. Linus Ullmark stopped 20 of 21. Stuart Skinner stopped 25 of 27 and got a loss for his trouble. The Senators have won three straight, and the Jets' six-game winning streak is over. Winnipeg had a heater on the line at home and put 21 shots on net, the offensive urgency of a team returning a library book.

Puckline's Report

Tampa Bay got Brayden Point, Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak back in the lineup and had a 3-0 lead before the Capitals finished stretching. Sam O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal 2:11 in, with Point picking up an assist, Charle-Edouard D'Astous made it two, and Jake Guentzel made it three at 13:11. Alex Tuch got one back, Guentzel scored again in the second for his 13th, Ryan Leonard made it 4-2 in the third, and Cirelli closed it into the empty net. John Carlson had three assists against his old team, because of course he did, and Nikita Kucherov had two in his 900th game. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 27; Logan Thompson stopped 20 of 24. Washington has lost three straight for the first time this season, and Alex Ovechkin's goal drought is at 14 games, tying the longest of his career. The man caught Gretzky. Right now he can't catch a break, a bounce or a Tuesday in Tampa.

Puckline's Report

Make it seven straight losses for the Maple Leafs, and this one came with a former Leaf doing the honors. Easton Cowan put Toronto up 3:22 in, and then the second period got silly: Frank Nazar scored twice, Teddy Blueger tied it 22 seconds after Nazar's second, and Connor Bedard put Chicago ahead for good 35 seconds after that. Tyler Bertuzzi made it 4-2 on a third-period power play, John Tavares cut it to one, and the Blackhawks answered in 12 seconds through Oliver Moore, then again 49 seconds later on Bertuzzi's second of the night. Sam Rinzel had three assists. Spencer Knight stopped 31 of 34; Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 19 of 25, a .760 that explains plenty. Toronto outshot Chicago 34-25 and lost by three. The Leafs have found the one thing harder to watch than their Aprils: their Novembers.

Puckline's Report

Fourteen goals, eight different Blues scorers, one Cutter Gauthier hat trick, and a final two minutes that should come with a seat belt. Gauthier scored his 19th, 20th and 21st to run his goal streak to 10 games, one short of Teemu Selanne's Ducks record, added an assist, and lost in regulation. St. Louis broke it open with three goals in 2:58 of the third, from Jake Neighbours, Philip Broberg and Logan Mailloux, whose first of the season capped a career-high three-point night. That made it 7-3 and ended Ville Husso's evening at seven goals on 24 shots. Anaheim then scored three straight, two with the net empty, to get within 7-6 with 41 seconds left, and Pavel Buchnevich hit the empty net three seconds later. Jordan Binnington allowed six on 31 in his first start since Nov. 5 and won comfortably, sort of. The Ducks scored six and never led. Defense in this one was a rumor nobody could confirm.

Puckline's Report

The Wild's point streak is at 12 games, and the Predators were kind enough to settle this one before the first intermission. Brock Faber scored his first of the season 4:20 in, Blake Coleman and Maxim Shabanov followed, and Matt Boldy made it 4-0 with 81 seconds left in the period, then 5-0 on the power play 59 seconds into the second. Nicolas Hague got Nashville on the board, Marcus Foligno answered 17 seconds later off a pass from brother Nick, and that was it for Justus Annunen: six goals on 20 shots. Juuse Saros stopped 17 of 18 in relief, a nice effort for a game already in the trash. Joel Eriksson Ek had a goal and three assists, Kirill Kaprizov had three assists, and Jesper Wallstedt stopped 25 of 28. Jonathan Marchessault scored in his return for Nashville, whose road trip ended like a bad night on Broadway: early, loud and with somebody getting pulled out of there.

Puckline's Report

Vegas led 3-1 with 78 seconds left and lost, a collapse so fast the building didn't have time to boo it properly. William Karlsson scored twice and Brett Howden added a third, and the Golden Knights were a minute and change from ending their skid. Then Dallas pulled Jake Oettinger: Wyatt Johnston scored at 18:42, Mikko Rantanen tied it with five seconds on the clock, and Miro Heiskanen, in his first game back after missing five, won it 3:36 into overtime. Rantanen had a goal and three assists, a point on every Stars goal, including Nils Lundkvist's first of the season. Oettinger stopped 24 of 27; Adin Hill stopped 18 of 22. That's three straight losses for Vegas, and the same two teams go again Thursday in the same building. The Knights had this one counted, cashed and halfway to the cage, then learned what every tourist on the Strip already knows: you're not up until you walk out the door.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

Jonathan Castagna showed up in San Jose without an NHL goal and left with two, and Simon Nemec scored his first as a Flame, so Calgary's equipment staff spent the night taping pucks. Adam Gaudette put the Sharks up 3:53 in, Matt Coronato tied it 76 seconds later, and Martin Pospisil gave Calgary the lead with 38 seconds left in the first. Nemec's power-play goal early in the second made it 3-1, and Castagna's first made it 4-1 in the third, with an assist to Maxim Tsyplakov in his first game after seven straight in the press box. Mason Marchment scored with the San Jose net empty and a power play going, and Castagna answered into the same empty net. Dustin Wolf stopped 21 of 23; Yaroslav Askarov stopped 24 of 28. The Sharks' future remains bright, mostly because it keeps getting pushed further away.

BOS @ DET · 7:30 PM ET

Boston BruinsBOS13-7-1 · 27 PTSML -110
@7:30 PM ETWed Nov 18 · Little Caesars Arena
BOS -110MLDET -110
Detroit Red WingsDET8-10-3 · 19 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

One hundred years ago tonight, on Nov. 18, 1926, a brand-new team called the Detroit Cougars played its first NHL game. It was in Windsor, Ontario, because Detroit didn't have a rink ready yet, and the Cougars lost 2-0 to the Boston Bruins. So for the Centennial Celebration Game the Red Wings have invited back the original party crashers, which is either lovely symmetry or tempting fate.

The 2026 Bruins don't look much like spoilers. Boston (13-7-1) has lost three straight, all at home and all by three or more goals, the latest a 3-0 loss to the Kings on Tuesday, the first shutout of the Marco Sturm era. The power play is 4-for-31 over nine games, and Sturm put David Pastrnak, Elias Lindholm and Morgan Geekie back together in the third period hunting for a spark. Now comes the second night of a back-to-back, with Jeremy Swayman the likely starter. Detroit (8-10-3) has its own mess: Alex DeBrincat and Viktor Arvidsson have each gone six games without a point, per Detroit Hockey Now, and rookie defenseman William Wallinder is out. But Daniil Tarasov and his .931 save percentage get the net after a 2-0 shutout in Tampa, and Lucas Raymond has 21 points in 21 games. Boston took three of four last season. A century later, somebody still has to score.

By Puckline Prince

MTL @ NJD · 7:30 PM ET

Montreal CanadiensMTL12-5-4 · 28 PTSML +146
@7:30 PM ETWed Nov 18 · Prudential Center
MTL +146MLNJD -178
New Jersey DevilsNJD15-6-0 · 30 PTSML -178

Puckline Preview

Not long ago Montreal was riding a 12-game point streak. Then came a 4-1 loss to Colorado and a 3-1 loss at Madison Square Garden that Martin St-Louis called one of his team's worst games of the year, and now the Canadiens (12-5-4) arrive in Newark with one goal in each of their last two and a power play ranked 31st at 12.5 percent. It was 10th last season. Somewhere in Brossard there's a whiteboard with a lot of eraser marks on it.

The Devils (15-6-0) are a rough place to go looking for a get-right game. They're 8-2 in their last 10, 9-2-0 at home, and fresh off a home-and-home sweep of Washington in which they scored 12 goals. Jack Hughes has 27 points in 21 games, Lenni Hameenaho has four points in two games since his recall, and Connor Hellebuyck is 7-0-0 in a Devils sweater. Neither team has named a goalie, and Montreal plays in Carolina on Thursday, so it's Jacob Fowler (9-2-2, .923) or Jakub Dobes. Brett Pesce looks ready to rejoin the New Jersey blue line. Last season's three meetings went overtime, shootout and a 3-0 Devils shutout in which Montreal managed 18 shots; the Canadiens never beat them in 60 minutes. The streak was fun. Newark is where fun goes to get audited.

By Puckline Prince

COL @ UTA · 10:00 PM ET

Colorado AvalancheCOL12-6-3 · 27 PTSML -102
@10:00 PM ETWed Nov 18 · Delta Center
COL -102MLUTA -118
Utah MammothUTA10-9-3 · 23 PTSML -118

Puckline Preview

Call it the Winter Classic dress rehearsal: these two meet outdoors on Dec. 31 at Rice-Eccles Stadium, and tonight neither one looks like the poster. The Avalanche (12-6-3) are without Nathan MacKinnon, out at least a month, and Cale Makar, out about two weeks, both hurt Nov. 12 in Ottawa. All Colorado did in its first game without them was beat Montreal 4-1. Artturi Lehkonen has 15 goals and Mackenzie Blackwood is 7-1-1 in his last nine starts, though with Anaheim on deck Thursday nobody has said which goalie plays tonight.

Utah (10-9-3) would trade problems in a heartbeat. The Mammoth started 10-6-0 and haven't won since Nov. 3: six straight losses (0-3-3), the latest a 3-2 home loss Monday to last-place Vancouver, decided on a Canucks power-play goal after Clayton Keller took a penalty during Utah's own power play. That's the Mammoth in miniature: a power play ranked third in the league, a penalty kill ranked 28th, and 103 penalties, third most in the NHL, to keep the wrong unit busy. Karel Vejmelka is 1-6-2 in his last nine starts. Logan Cooley, at least, is back, with 11 goals. Colorado went 3-0-1 against Utah last season, and this is the first meeting of the new one. The outdoor game can wait. Utah needs an indoor win first.

By Puckline Prince
